verdict_reasoning: The proposal fails at level 1b on maintenance-fit-1 and already-exists-1. COPY TO '/dev/null' already runs the same check, and the thread gives no reason for a permanent COPY keyword beyond 11-14% less CPU. The author accepts in message #6 that pg_dump is the wrong place and considers a client-only pg_amcheck option, which would be a different proposal. Confidence is medium because v1 has no documentation and the pg_amcheck alternative has no design.

brief.title: COPY TO BLACKHOLE and a pg_dump blackhole format for parallel checks
brief.problem: Users check for corruption with COPY to '/dev/null' or verify_heapam(), and the author says each finds different kinds of corruption. pg_dump -j works only with -Fd, so a parallel logical check of a large database needs disk space for the whole dump.
brief.proposed_design: Patch 0001 adds a BLACKHOLE destination to COPY TO that reads and forms all rows but sends no output, which saves some CPU. Patch 0002 adds a pg_dump archive format, -Fb, that uses COPY TO BLACKHOLE in parallel mode and writes nothing. In message #6 the author considers moving the parallel part to pg_amcheck instead of pg_dump.
user_visible_surface: SQL syntax: COPY <table> TO BLACKHOLE, with BLACKHOLE as a new keyword in kwlist.h.
pg_dump option: new archive format -Fb (blackhole), allowed with -j.
COPY progress reporting: progress.h is touched, but the patch prose does not say what changes.
author_claims: COPY TO BLACKHOLE is about 1.14x faster than COPY to '/dev/null' on a hot cache and about 1.11x on a cold cache, on pgbench_accounts with 10M rows.
COPY TO BLACKHOLE on a cold cache was faster than verify_heapam() with check_toast => true.
COPY tests TOAST harder than amcheck: the attached script shows corrupt pglz data that verify_heapam() misses and COPY reports.
The added check in the COPY row path is one predictable branch, so it costs close to nothing.
pg_dump -j -Fb gives a parallel logical check of the whole database with no disk space used.
brief.thread_state: Ahmed and Miłosz find both COPY and pg_dump the wrong place for this, Hannu Krosing suggests COPY to '/dev/null' or a hashtext query, and Michael Paquier asks for better corruption tools instead and warns about cost in the COPY path. The author agrees pg_dump is wrong and is choosing between withdrawing and a pg_amcheck option; no new version was posted.
unclear: v1 has no documentation, and the author planned none until the idea had support.
No benchmark shows the cost of the new branch for normal COPY TO with other schemas or data patterns.
The material does not say how the hot-cache savings arise, given that COPY to '/dev/null' already discards output.
The condition shown tests whereToSendOutput == DestRemote, and the prose does not say how BLACKHOLE behaves for file or program targets.
No design is given for the pg_amcheck alternative: option name, use of core COPY, or client-only work.
The proposal does not say which corruption the COPY check finds that indexes, catalogs or pg_catcheck do not cover.

objections.title: A COPY destination for corruption checks does not belong in COPY
objections.failure_scenario: Postgres adds BLACKHOLE as a COPY keyword and destination to gain about 14% over COPY TO '/dev/null'. Users then rely on COPY as a supported corruption checker. If amcheck later gains detoast checks, the syntax still has to stay for compatibility.
objections.argument: Message #2 says a COPY destination that moves no data is counter-intuitive. Message #4 notes that '/dev/null' or a hashtext query already does the same work, and in message #5 Michael Paquier asks for better corruption tools instead. In message #6 the author suggests a client-only pg_amcheck option that would not touch core COPY, which fits existing practice better.
objections.author_must_show: What does COPY TO BLACKHOLE offer that a pg_amcheck option running COPY TO '/dev/null' or a full-row query in parallel cannot offer?

critic.reasoning: Messages #2, #4 and #5 object to the placement, and message #6 offers a client-only pg_amcheck option that leaves core COPY alone. The material gives no reason beyond 11-14% less CPU for a permanent COPY destination.

objections.title: COPY TO '/dev/null' already gives the same check
objections.failure_scenario: Postgres adds a second COPY TO destination that forms every row and discards it, as COPY TO '/dev/null' already does. Every later change to the COPY TO row path has to keep the BLACKHOLE branch working. The only gain is about 11-14% on a check that users run rarely.
objections.argument: Message #1 shows that COPY to '/dev/null' runs the same check, and message #6's pglz reproducer shows it catches the same TOAST corruption that BLACKHOLE targets. Message #4 makes the same point, and the thread never answers it. Users without pg_write_server_files can run COPY TO STDOUT with output sent to /dev/null on the client. Parallel runs need no core change, because N sessions or a pg_amcheck-style client driver can each run COPY to '/dev/null', and message #6 itself names the client-only option "--copy-to-null".
objections.author_must_show: Which check can BLACKHOLE do that COPY TO '/dev/null' or COPY TO STDOUT from a parallel client cannot, beyond about 12% less CPU?

critic.reasoning: Message #6 shows COPY TO '/dev/null' reporting the same pglz error, and parallel client sessions need no core change. The thread does not answer message #4, and the author names a client-only "--copy-to-null" option.

other_surviving.title: New COPY destination keyword where an option or existing target would do
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A user writes COPY t TO blackhole and expects a destination, but the command exists only to check that rows can be read. If a later version moves this check to amcheck or renames it COPY VERIFY, as message #3 suggests, scripts written against TO BLACKHOLE must change and the keyword stays in the grammar.
other_surviving.argument: COPY TO today takes a file name, PROGRAM or STDOUT, and its other behaviour lives in the WITH (...) option list, so a new grammar keyword departs from that practice. Message #2 calls the destination counter-intuitive, and Hannu notes in message #4 that '/dev/null' already serves the purpose. The author is still open on the name (message #3) and is weighing a client-only pg_amcheck option that would not touch COPY (message #6). Fixing a spelling in the SQL grammar before that choice is made puts the project behind a contract it may not keep.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Why is a new BLACKHOLE keyword in the COPY grammar needed, when a COPY option, '/dev/null', or a pg_amcheck flag would cover the same check?

critic.reasoning: Patch 0001 adds BLACKHOLE to kwlist.h and gram.y, and message #3 shows the name is still open. No message says why a COPY option or a client-only pg_amcheck flag would not do.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: Visible COPY contract for BLACKHOLE is not defined
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A monitoring tool reads pg_stat_progress_copy and finds a type value it does not know, or a role with only SELECT runs COPY TO BLACKHOLE and gets results that differ from COPY TO '/dev/null'. Users find these differences only after the release, because v1 has no documentation.
other_surviving.argument: The patch touches progress.h, and its prose does not say what pg_stat_progress_copy shows for a BLACKHOLE copy. The proposal also does not say which privilege COPY TO BLACKHOLE needs, compared with pg_write_server_files for COPY TO a file. The condition quoted in message #6 tests DestRemote, and the proposal does not say what happens in other sessions. Message #1 says no documentation is planned until the idea has support, so these user-facing parts of the contract have no written definition yet.
other_surviving.author_must_show: What do pg_stat_progress_copy, privilege checks and non-client sessions show or require for COPY TO BLACKHOLE, and where is that documented?

critic.reasoning: Missing documentation alone is out of scope, and the monitoring scenario is a guess. But the proposal does not say which privilege BLACKHOLE needs or what it does when whereToSendOutput is not DestRemote, and both are design questions.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: No measurement of the new branch for ordinary COPY TO
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A user who runs large COPY TO STDOUT exports, with wide or many-column tables, pays the new per-row check on every row. Nobody measures this before release, so a regression shows up only in field reports.
other_surviving.argument: The only numbers in message #1 compare BLACKHOLE with '/dev/null' on pgbench_accounts. Michael Paquier warns in message #5 that row-level additions show up depending on schema and data pattern. The author's reply in message #6 says the branch is predictable, but gives no measurement for COPY users who do not use BLACKHOLE.
other_surviving.author_must_show: What is the cost to normal COPY TO STDOUT and COPY TO file, in text and binary format, on narrow and wide tables?

critic.reasoning: Message #6 answers the cost concern from message #5 with an argument about branch prediction and no numbers. The only benchmark compares BLACKHOLE with '/dev/null' on pgbench_accounts, so the cost for normal COPY TO is unmeasured.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

refuted.title: Check coverage depends on COPY internals that nobody guards
refuted.failure_scenario: A later COPY TO optimization skips detoasting or output-function calls when output is discarded. BLACKHOLE then stops reporting the pglz corruption shown in message #6. No test fails, and users learn about it only when a check passes on a corrupt table.
refuted.argument: The value of the feature comes from side effects of COPY's output path, as the TOAST case in message #6 shows. The proposal does not state which checks BLACKHOLE promises to do. Future COPY changes, such as new formats or faster paths, would have to keep those side effects working without any contract that says so.
refuted.author_must_show: Which checks does BLACKHOLE guarantee, and what test fails if a later COPY change stops detoasting or calling output functions?

critic.reasoning: The scenario needs a later optimization that nobody has proposed, and it would have to remove the row forming that the commit message gives as the feature's purpose. The same risk applies to any code a later patch might change.

refuted.title: Gain over the existing COPY to '/dev/null' workaround is small
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator checking a suspect cluster can run COPY t TO '/dev/null' today and see the same pglz error message #6 shows. With BLACKHOLE the same check finishes about 11-14% sooner. Postgres then carries a new keyword and COPY syntax for that difference.
refuted.argument: Message #1 shows a 1.14x hot-cache gain and a 1.11x cold-cache gain, and message #6 shows the corruption found through COPY to '/dev/null' and through SELECT. Message #4 points to COPY to '/dev/null' and a hashtext query as existing ways to force full tuple construction. The only demand in the material is the author's own support work, and no -general or -bugs reports appear. Message #2 also finds the COPY placement ad hoc.
refuted.author_must_show: Which users run corruption checks where a 11-14% speedup over COPY to '/dev/null' changes what they can do, and how many such reports exist?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of already-exists-1. Its extra claim of no demand does not hold for the check itself, because message #5 calls pg_dump and COPY a popular way to check data state.

refuted.title: COPY TO users pay for a check that few people run
refuted.failure_scenario: Every COPY TO, including the bulk exports that ETL jobs and pg_dump run, goes through the new branch in the per-row path. If a schema or data pattern makes this cost show up, every COPY user pays it. The occasional corruption check is the only beneficiary.
refuted.argument: Message #5 warns that additions to the COPY row path are never free and depend on schema and data pattern. Message #6 answers that the branch is predictable, but no benchmark of normal COPY TO with other schemas is shown. The gain goes to a small group, while all COPY TO workloads take on the cost and the code path.
refuted.author_must_show: Can benchmarks of normal COPY TO across narrow and wide tables show no measurable cost from the new branch?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-2, which states the same unmeasured per-row cost and asks for the same benchmark in more detail.

touch_points.label: wire protocol
touch_points.reason: COPY TO BLACKHOLE sends no row data to the client, and the proposal does not say which COPY messages the client receives.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: Patch 0001 changes copy.h and parsenodes.h and touches the test_copy_callbacks module.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: Patch 0001 adds BLACKHOLE to kwlist.h and to the COPY TO grammar.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: Patch 0002 adds an archive format, -Fb, that writes nothing and cannot be restored.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: The proposal does not say which privilege COPY TO BLACKHOLE needs, while COPY to '/dev/null' needs pg_write_server_files.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: A new keyword, a new COPY destination and a new pg_dump archive format must be kept working after commit.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: The patch adds a branch to the per-row path of every COPY TO, with no benchmark for normal COPY TO.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: COPY to '/dev/null' from parallel client sessions already gives the same check with no core change.

questions: What does COPY TO BLACKHOLE offer that a pg_amcheck option running COPY TO '/dev/null' or COPY TO STDOUT in parallel sessions cannot, beyond 11-14% less CPU?
Where do the hot-cache savings come from, given that COPY to '/dev/null' already discards the output?
If the pg_amcheck route is chosen, what is the option name, and does it need any change to core COPY?
Which corruption does a COPY-based check find that verify_heapam() with check_toast, index checks and pg_catcheck do not cover?
What does the new per-row branch cost normal COPY TO STDOUT and COPY TO file, in text and binary format, on narrow and wide tables?

committability.owner_note: It needs someone who knows the COPY TO row path and, for the alternative, pg_amcheck. Michael Paquier raised the COPY path cost in message #5, but nobody has offered to take the patch.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a new SQL keyword and COPY destination that must stay for compatibility, a per-row branch in every COPY TO, and a pg_dump archive format that archives nothing.
committability.author_follow_up: The author replied within a day in message #3 and offered to write a new version, but no new version was posted and withdrawal is under consideration.

priority.reason: The goal of a parallel logical check with no disk use is valid for large databases, and the two patches are small. Reviewers and the author agree the COPY and pg_dump placement is wrong, so a client-only pg_amcheck option needs its own proposal.

provisional_note: The level 2 objections on syntax, privileges, progress reporting and per-row cost were not evaluated because level 1b fails. The code was not read, so the behaviour for file and program targets and the size of the CPU saving are unverified.

precedents_retrieved.title: Verify true root on replicas with amcheck
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets the regular bt_check_index() function in amcheck verify the true root of a B-Tree index, so the check also works on replicas. It does this by locking the metapage and the potential root page at the same time.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author stopped responding. Peter Geoghegan asked what true root corruption meant and what symptom it caused, and he did not want to commit a patch that holds multiple buffer locks without a strong justification. The patch also stopped applying, and David Steele returned it after no reply from the author.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Your patch looks like it gets it right (it won't deadlock with other
sessions that access the metapage), but I hesitate to commit it
without a strong justification.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow pg_verify_checksums to specify a database to scan
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add options to pg_verify_checksums to limit checksum verification to one database, given by OID with -d/--dboid, or to shared relations only with -g/--global-only. This follows a discussion that the existing -r RELFILENODE option had no way to say which database it referred to.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Fabien COELHO's review asked for several changes: TAP tests (the command had none), stricter parsing of the OID argument, handling of -d and -g given together (that combination succeeded while checking nothing), and documentation fixes. Masahiko Sawada suggested allowing several database OIDs. The thread ends with these review comments and shows no revised patch before the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: When the command is started with both "-d 1 -g", it succeeds by checking nothing, which is quite misleading. Probably it should complain that these options are mutually exclusive, or it should check both under -g AND -d 1?

precedents_retrieved.title: amcheck verification for GiST
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a GiST verification function to contrib/amcheck that checks parent/child key consistency and that all leaf pages are at the same depth. Later versions hold buffer locks on parent and child pages together and take only an AccessShareLock on the relation.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Geoghegan questioned whether the checks are safe under an AccessShareLock, since Heikki's v6 had used a ShareLock. He doubted that the parent re-find logic copied from gistfinishsplit() applies here and asked how concurrent page deletion could affect it. Andrey Borodin did not answer these questions for about two months, so Michael Paquier returned the entry with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: My main concern now is the heavyweight lock strength needed by the new function.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_dump: optimize dumpFunc()
precedents_retrieved.summary: Replace pg_dump's per-function query in dumpFunc() with a single query that gathers data for all functions up front, keeping the PGresult in memory and using a sorted array of function OIDs to locate each function's row. The aim was to reduce dump time for databases with many functions (shown as about 0.25s to about 0.11s for 10k simple functions).
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane questioned whether the change helps databases with few functions and what it does to pg_dump's memory requirements when there are very many functions with large source text, and said the shown results did not justify the risk. The author agreed and withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm not sure that the results you're showing justify taking any
risk here.

precedents_retrieved.title: Check for tuplestorestate nullness before dereferencing
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a NULL check on tuplestorestate in ExecMaterial (nodeMaterial.c) before tuplestore_advance() is called. The author based it on an existing NULL check used when computing eof_tuplestore.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane judged the check unnecessary: the backward-scan path runs only when EXEC_FLAG_BACKWARD was given, and that flag makes the node create a tuplestore. He objected that a silent check would hide a real bug and suggested an Assert instead. The entry was then withdrawn, and the visible messages show no revised patch.

precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
But I don't like the proposed patch because if tuplestore is
null here, something's wrong, and we should complain not
silently mask the problem.

precedents_retrieved.title: Align verify_heapam.c error message offset with test expectations
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes three error messages in contrib/amcheck/verify_heapam.c to report the successor tuple's offset (nextoffnum) instead of the current line pointer (ctx.offnum). A second part tightens the pg_amcheck test 004_verify_heapam.pl to expect the exact offset 43 instead of a \d+ wildcard.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Two reviewers agreed with the code fix, and no one objected. The author said he would not revise the test change further and left the decision to committers, and the thread ends there.

precedents_retrieved.title: Check for TupleTableSlot nullness before dereferencing
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Daniel Gustafsson, Jacob Champion, David Rowley
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a null check on a TupleTableSlot in process_ordered_aggregate_multi() in nodeAgg.c before it is dereferenced. The author argued that slot1 and slot2 can be swapped, so a null slot2 could reach the dereference.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers did not see how the null dereference can happen. In build_pertrans_for_aggref(), uniqslot is always allocated when numDistinctCols > 0, and the swap of slot1 and slot2 only happens under that same condition. Jacob Champion asked for a test case that shows the crash, and none was posted before the entry was withdrawn.

uniqslot is created in
build_pertrans_for_aggref() when "numDistinctCols > 0", and the swap
of slot1 and slot2 also only occurs when "numDistinctCols > 0".

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve amcheck to check UNIQUE constraint in btree index
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Peter Geoghegan, Mark Dilger, David Steele
precedents_retrieved.summary: Extend contrib/amcheck's bt_index_check and bt_index_parent_check so that, for btree indexes with a UNIQUE constraint, they detect duplicate keys whose heap tuples are visible, including duplicates spanning adjacent leaf pages, and report the index and heap TIDs involved. Later versions added an optional argument to enable the uniqueness check and a regression test variant for 32-bit systems.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers asked for further changes: Peter Geoghegan objected to reporting violations as WARNINGs, to the message saying an index only might be corrupt (calling it an unacceptable false positive), to the handling of cross-page duplicates, and to tests that update pg_index, and suggested opclass-based fault injection and sharing the heapallindexed snapshot. Mark Dilger's review of v4 asked for documentation updates, pg_amcheck integration with TAP tests, and a different test approach. No updated patch followed for several weeks, and David Steele marked it Returned with Feedback because it needed more work and had not been updated.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This patch appears to need some work and has not been updated in several
weeks, so marking Returned with Feedback.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the index returned no earlier attempt at a discard-only COPY target or an output-free pg_dump format. Message #6 links earlier threads about pg_catcheck reading only the first row of each relation, but the material does not report a rejection reason there that applies to this proposal.
The pg_dump -Fb archive format is not raised here: message #2 objected to it and the author accepted that point in message #6.

The proposal adds no persistent or cross-node state. It changes no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog, replication path or extension-facing struct, and the -Fb format writes no archive for pg_restore to read. The open questions are the client messages for COPY TO BLACKHOLE under DestRemote and what progress.h changes, and the prose does not answer either.

No security objection: COPY TO BLACKHOLE reads only what COPY TO STDOUT or a SELECT already lets a user with SELECT privilege read, and it writes nothing to the server file system. It also needs less privilege than COPY to '/dev/null', which needs pg_write_server_files. The prose does not say which privilege check BLACKHOLE uses, how it handles row-level security, or what progress reporting exposes, and these need checking in the code.
I do not repeat the pg_dump -Fb objection. The author accepted in message #6 that pg_dump is the wrong place for this.
The pg_dump -Fb format is not raised, because message #6 already accepts that pg_dump is the wrong place.

The parallel need is real for large databases, but the author already accepts in message #6 that pg_dump is the wrong place. A pg_amcheck option with no core change has no design yet and was not evaluated.
